```{python}
#| tags: [setup]
import sys, os
sys.path.insert(0, os.path.abspath("."))
from _pcpkg import *  # noqa: F401,F403
import doe_report as D
import matplotlib.pyplot as plt

DOC = "PCR-007"
UO = "cex"
UO_TITLE = "Cation Exchange Chromatography (Step 7)"
# CEX sets no CQA of its own; it is the principal aggregate-reduction (polish) step and
# a major clearance step for HCP, residual DNA and leached Protein A. cqas_for(UO) is
# empty, so the CQAs it controls/clears are listed explicitly.
CEX_CQAS = ["aggregates_hmw", "hcp", "residual_dna", "leached_protein_a"]
n_scr = doe_runs(UO, "screening")
n_rsm = doe_runs(UO, "rsm")

# The two quality responses (eluate-pool aggregate and HCP) carry the systematic
# parameter structure and define the operating region; step yield is governed by protein
# load and is otherwise robust (its full-quadratic predicted R² is lower because only the
# load main effect is active over the ranges studied).
MODELED = ["aggregate_out_pct", "hcp_out_ng_mg"]
agg_fit = D.fit(UO, "rsm", "aggregate_out_pct")
hcp_fit = D.fit(UO, "rsm", "hcp_out_ng_mg")
AGG_R2, HCP_R2 = agg_fit["R2"], hcp_fit["R2"]
R2_MODELED_MIN = min(AGG_R2, HCP_R2)
R2_MODELED_MAX = max(AGG_R2, HCP_R2)
ADJ_MODELED_MIN = min(agg_fit["adjR2"], hcp_fit["adjR2"])
PRED_MODELED_MIN = min(agg_fit["predR2"], hcp_fit["predR2"])
LOF_PS = [D.fit(UO, "rsm", r)["p_lof"] for r in MODELED]
LOF_MODELED_NS = all((p != p) or (p > 0.05) for p in LOF_PS)   # NaN-safe "all non-significant"

cc = D.center_cv_df(UO, "rsm")
def _cc(key, col="Mean"):
    return float(cc.loc[cc.Response == D.RESP_LABEL[key], col].iloc[0])
AGG_CENTER = _cc("aggregate_out_pct")
HCP_CENTER = _cc("hcp_out_ng_mg")

# Nominal-batch clearance (self-consistent output + fold from the process summary).
ps = csv("process_summary.csv")
cex_ps = ps[ps.unit_operation == "Cation Exchange Chromatography"].iloc[0]
AGG_OUT = float(cex_ps.aggregate_out_pct)
HCP_OUT = float(cex_ps.hcp_out_ng_mg)
AGG_FOLD = float(cex_ps.aggregate_clearance_fold)
HCP_FOLD = float(cex_ps.hcp_clearance_fold)

yw = csv("yield_waterfall.csv")
CEX_YIELD = float(yw[yw.step == 7].iloc[0].step_yield)
agg_acc_hi = cqa_reg[cqa_reg.key == "aggregates_hmw"].iloc[0].acc_high
hcp_acc_hi = int(cqa_reg[cqa_reg.key == "hcp"].iloc[0].acc_high)
agg_cpk = float(cap[cap.key == "aggregates_hmw"].iloc[0].Cpk)
hcp_cpk = float(cap[cap.key == "hcp"].iloc[0].Cpk)
dna_cpk = float(cap[cap.key == "residual_dna"].iloc[0].Cpk)
lpa_cpk = float(cap[cap.key == "leached_protein_a"].iloc[0].Cpk)
load = CFG.unit_op(UO).param("load")
wash = CFG.unit_op(UO).param("wash_cond")
```

# Executive summary {.unnumbered}

This report documents the Stage 1 (Process Design) characterization of the A-Mab
cation-exchange (CEX) polishing chromatography step (Step 7), the bind-and-elute
polishing operation that follows low-pH viral inactivation and is the **principal
aggregate-reduction step** of the purification train — the only step that actively
reduces high-molecular-weight aggregate — as well as a major clearance step for
host-cell protein (HCP) and a modular clearance step for residual DNA and leached
Protein A. The study was executed under the Process Characterization Plan **PCP-007** on
a qualified scale-down chromatography column, following the lifecycle approach to process
validation [@fda2011; @pdatr60; @ispegpg2023] and the Quality-by-Design principles of
ICH Q8, Q9 and Q11 [@ichq8; @ichq9; @ichq11], with the process model,
quality-attribute framework and risk methodology of the A-Mab case study [@amab2009].

Five process parameters were evaluated. A `{python} n_scr`-run two-level full factorial
screening design identified the significant factors and two-factor interactions for the
eluate-pool aggregate, the eluate-pool HCP and the step yield; a `{python} n_rsm`-run
face-centred central-composite response-surface design then quantified main effects,
interactions and curvature and defined the multivariate operating region in the
well-controlled CPPs. The aggregate and pool-HCP response-surface models are adequate and
predictive (R² = `{python} f"{R2_MODELED_MIN:.2f}"`–`{python} f"{R2_MODELED_MAX:.2f}"`,
adjusted R² ≥ `{python} f"{ADJ_MODELED_MIN:.2f}"`, predicted R² ≥
`{python} f"{PRED_MODELED_MIN:.2f}"`); the step yield is governed by protein load and is
otherwise robust.

```{python}
  stop-collect drive the eluate-pool aggregate, and the load/wash conductivity and protein
  load drive the eluate-pool HCP through a significant load × conductivity interaction.
  The elution flow rate has no product-quality or performance impact over its range and is
  **GPP**; there are no key process parameters (KPP) at this step.
- Aggregate rises with higher protein load, higher elution pH and a later stop-collect and
  is insensitive to the wash conductivity; the step reduces the pool aggregate by

  well below the {agg_acc_hi:g}% drug-substance limit.
- HCP clearance improves with higher load/wash conductivity and falls at high load; the
  step reduces the pool HCP by approximately **{HCP_FOLD:.0f}-fold** to about
  **{HCP_OUT:,.0f} ng/mg** at the nominal condition, which the anion-exchange step further
  polishes to the ≤ {hcp_acc_hi} ng/mg drug-substance limit.
- The nominal step recovers **{pct(CEX_YIELD)}** of the loaded product; yield declines
  modestly at high load and is otherwise robust.
- A multivariate operating region in the four well-controlled CPPs was established over
  which the eluate-pool aggregate and HCP are controlled so that the integrated control
  strategy delivers in-specification drug substance, with a commercial-scale aggregate
  capability of **Cpk = {agg_cpk:.2f}** — the step being the principal contributor to the
  drug-substance aggregate outcome.
""")
```

The cation-exchange step is demonstrated to be well understood and robust. The operating
region, parameter classifications and proven acceptable ranges support the Stage 2
operating ranges and the drug-substance control strategy, and this report rolls up into
the Process Characterization Master Report (**PCMR-001**).

# Introduction

## Product and unit operation

A-Mab is a humanized IgG1 monoclonal antibody purified by a platform
Protein A → low-pH viral-inactivation → cation-exchange → anion-exchange →
virus-filtration → UF/DF train [@amab2009]. Cation-exchange chromatography is the first
polishing step: the neutralized viral-inactivation pool is loaded onto a strong
cation-exchange resin at controlled conductivity, weakly bound impurities are removed in
the wash, and the product is recovered by elution, with the eluate pool collected between
defined start and stop criteria. The step forms no new product-quality CQA; its role in
the control strategy is to reduce the high-molecular-weight aggregate carried into the
pool — including the aggregate that can arise during the upstream low-pH hold — and to
provide a major further reduction of HCP and modular clearance of residual DNA and
leached Protein A. This characterization quantifies how the polishing parameters govern
the eluate-pool aggregate, the eluate-pool HCP and the step yield.

## Objectives

The objectives of the study were to (i) establish the quantitative relationships between
the cation-exchange process parameters and the eluate-pool aggregate, the eluate-pool HCP
and the step yield; (ii) define the multivariate operating region over which the
aggregate and HCP presented to the anion-exchange step are controlled; (iii) establish
proven acceptable ranges (PARs) and normal operating ranges (NORs) for each parameter;
(iv) classify each parameter for its risk of impact to CQAs and to process performance;
and (v) provide the process understanding and ranges that justify the Stage 2 operating
conditions and the control strategy.

## Regulatory and scientific basis

The work follows the lifecycle approach to process validation of the FDA 2011 guidance
[@fda2011], PDA Technical Report 60 [@pdatr60] and the ISPE Good Practice Guide
[@ispegpg2023], and applies the enhanced (QbD) development approach of ICH Q8, Q9 and Q11
[@ichq8; @ichq9; @ichq11]. Criticality is treated as a continuum (ICH Q9). The report
structure corresponds to the Stage 1 Process Design Report of PDA TR 60 §3.11 and provides
development-report content suitable to support a Biologics License Application.

# Prior knowledge and quality risk basis

## Platform and prior-product knowledge

Cation-exchange polishing is a platform operation whose behaviour is well established from
related humanized IgG1 antibodies (X-Mab, Y-Mab and Z-Mab) and from A-Mab clinical and
engineering experience [@amab2009]. Prior knowledge established that aggregate, being more
highly charged and more strongly retained than monomer, is resolved from monomer in the
elution so that the eluate-pool aggregate rises with higher protein load, with a later
stop-collect (which extends the pool further down the descending edge into the
late-eluting aggregate) and at higher elution pH; that HCP clearance is governed by the
load/wash conductivity — a higher conductivity strips more weakly bound HCP before the
elution — and falls at high load, the two acting together through a load × conductivity
interaction; and that recovery declines modestly at high load. This knowledge framed the
attributes in scope and the prioritization of parameters for characterization.

## Quality attributes in scope

Cation exchange introduces no CQA. It is the principal reduction step for the
high-molecular-weight aggregate and a major clearance step for the impurity CQAs formed
upstream and specified at the drug substance: host-cell protein, residual DNA and leached
Protein A (@tbl-cqa). Criticality is scored on the A-Mab continuum using Tool #1 (Risk
Score = Impact × Uncertainty); attributes rated High (H) or Very High (VH) are treated as
*Critical* [@amab2009].

```{python}
#| output: asis
show(cqas_by_keys(CEX_CQAS))
```

: CQAs controlled by the cation-exchange step (formed upstream; polished/cleared here), with acceptance criterion and criticality (Tool #1 = Impact × Uncertainty). {#tbl-cqa}

The eluate-pool aggregate and eluate-pool HCP are not themselves released specifications;
they are in-process attributes whose control at this step determines the size-variant and
impurity load presented to the anion-exchange step and therefore the margin to the
≤ `{python} f"{agg_acc_hi:g}"`% HMW aggregate and ≤ `{python} hcp_acc_hi` ng/mg HCP
drug-substance limits. Because aggregate can be elevated in the incoming pool, the study
was designed to demonstrate the aggregate-clearance capacity of the step against a
representative, deliberately challenging aggregate feed; pool aggregate is characterized
here as the primary response of the study.

## Risk-based prioritization and parameter selection

Consistent with the A-Mab lifecycle of iterative risk assessments, the characterization
scope was set by the Pre-Characterization Process Risk Assessment (**RA-001**), which used
prior knowledge and a risk-ranking-and-filtering screen to prioritize parameters and to
assign the study type. Protein load, load/wash conductivity, elution pH and the elution
stop-collect, which carry a credible main-effect and interaction risk to the eluate-pool
aggregate or HCP, were assigned to the multivariate DoE; the elution flow rate, expected
to affect only process performance over a wide range, was assigned to univariate
assessment [@amab2009; @pdatr60]. The parameters and ranges carried into this study are
given in @tbl-param (§5.1).

# Materials and methods

## Scale-down model and its qualification

All characterization runs were performed on a qualified scale-down cation-exchange column
operated at the commercial-process equivalents for resin, bed height, residence time,
buffer system, load ratio and elution strategy (**SOP-2010**, **SOP-2008**). The SDM was
qualified against at-scale reference data (**SOP-1001**) by comparing the operational
parameters and, critically, the input and output attributes — step yield, eluate-pool
aggregate and HCP, residual DNA and leached Protein A — confirming that the model is
representative and suitable to support operating-range and PAR claims [@pdatr60]. The
between-run reproducibility of the centre-point condition (§6.1) provides a direct
estimate of model precision and is used as the pure-error term in the lack-of-fit
assessment of every response-surface model.

## Operation

The neutralized viral-inactivation pool is conditioned to the target load conductivity
and loaded onto the equilibrated cation-exchange column to the target load ratio; the
column is washed at the load/wash conductivity to remove weakly bound host-cell protein
and other impurities; and the product is recovered by elution, with the eluate pool
collected from a defined start until the descending-edge stop-collect criterion. Buffers,
resin lot and column packing are controlled to platform specifications (**SOP-2008**) and
are treated as identity/quality-controlled inputs rather than characterized variables,
consistent with the A-Mab platform approach [@amab2009].

## Analytical methods

The step responses were measured by validated methods (@tbl-methods). Aggregate was
determined by SEC-HPLC (**AMV-3011**), the primary assay for the aggregate-polish claim;
host-cell protein by ELISA (**AMV-3012**); residual host-cell DNA by qPCR (**AMV-3014**);
and leached Protein A by ELISA (**AMV-3016**). Step yield was determined from the load and
eluate product mass by protein A₂₈₀. Method performance characteristics are summarized in
Appendix D.

```{python}
#| output: asis
print(sop_table(sops=[], amvs=CEX_AMV_REFS))
```

: Validated analytical methods used in the characterization. {#tbl-methods}

## Sampling plan

Each DoE run was sampled at the eluate pool for aggregate, HCP, residual DNA and leached
Protein A, and the load and pool product mass were recorded for the step-yield
determination; in-process readings (pH, conductivity, UV) confirmed the chromatographic
profile and the pool collection window. Centre-point runs were replicated within each
design (three in screening, four in the response-surface design) to quantify
reproducibility and pure error.

## Statistical methods

Designs were constructed and analyzed in coded factors, with each parameter's
characterization range mapped so that the set-point is 0 and the range edges are
±1 (**SOP-1002**). Screening data were analyzed by ordinary-least-squares regression of
each response on the main effects and all two-factor interactions; factor *effects* are
reported as twice the coded coefficient. Response-surface data were analyzed with the full
quadratic model (main effects, two-factor interactions and pure-quadratic terms).
Statistical significance was assessed at α = 0.05. Model adequacy was judged by the
coefficient of determination (R²), the adjusted R², the predicted R² (computed from the
PRESS statistic by leave-one-out), the overall model F-test, and an analysis of variance
partitioning the residual into lack of fit and pure error, the latter estimated from the
replicated centre points; a non-significant lack-of-fit F-test (p > 0.05) indicates an
adequate model. A response governed by a single dominant factor is reported by that
dependence and treated as otherwise robust rather than as a full predictive surface. The
operating region was defined as the multivariate region of the well-controlled CPPs over
which the eluate-pool aggregate and HCP are controlled. Commercial-scale process
capability for the drug-substance CQAs governed by the step was estimated by Monte-Carlo
simulation of `{python} f"{V['n_monte_carlo']:,}"` batches with each parameter varied
within its NOR, reporting the one-sided process-capability index (Cpk) for the impurity
and size-variant CQAs.

# Study design

## Factors, ranges and the knowledge space

Five parameters were studied (@tbl-param). The characterization range of each factor
("PAR" column) defines the edges of the explored knowledge space and the basis of the
proven acceptable range; the NOR is the tighter range at which the parameter is controlled
routinely. The DoE factor coding for the four multivariate factors is given in
@tbl-legend.


: Design-of-experiments factor legend (coded A–D). {#tbl-legend}

## Screening design

Factor screening used a two-level full factorial in the four multivariate factors (A–D)
with three centre-point replicates, `{python} n_scr` runs in total. The full factorial
estimates all four main effects and all six two-factor interactions without confounding.
The three responses recorded for each run were the eluate-pool aggregate, the eluate-pool
HCP and the step yield. The complete coded design matrix and run responses are given in
Appendix A.

## Response-surface design

The four multivariate factors were carried into a face-centred central-composite design
(cube points, axial points at the face centres, and four centre-point replicates),
`{python} n_rsm` runs in total, enabling estimation of curvature in addition to main
effects and interactions. The complete coded design matrix and responses are given in
Appendix B.

## Univariate assessment

The elution flow rate was evaluated one factor at a time across its characterization range
for its effect on step yield, the eluate-pool aggregate and HCP, and the chromatographic
profile; it was not carried into the multivariate design because prior knowledge indicated
no credible impact to a product-quality CQA.

point (@tbl-cv) is the pure-error estimate used in the lack-of-fit assessment; the

: Largest standardized effects on eluate-pool HCP (screening). {#tbl-eff-hcp}

Protein load, elution pH and the elution stop-collect are the active factors for the
eluate-pool aggregate — the pool aggregate rises with each — with significant
load × elution-pH and load × stop-collect interactions; the wash conductivity has no
significant effect on aggregate. The eluate-pool HCP, by contrast, is governed by the
load/wash conductivity and the protein load, with a significant load × conductivity
interaction: HCP clearance improves at higher conductivity and worsens at higher load, and
the interaction means the conductivity matters most when the column is heavily loaded. The
step yield is governed by protein load alone (recovery declines modestly at higher load)
and shows no other significant dependence. The aggregate and HCP responses therefore
respond to a partly shared set of factors, which is why a multivariate operating region —
rather than independent one-dimensional ranges — is used to assure the size-variant and
impurity load presented downstream.

`{python} f"{ADJ_MODELED_MIN:.2f}"`, and predicted R² ≥ `{python} f"{PRED_MODELED_MIN:.2f}"`,
indicating good predictive capability rather than overfitting.

## Mechanistic interpretation

The response-surface models reproduce the established behaviour of cation-exchange
polishing. High-molecular-weight aggregate carries a higher net positive charge and binds
the resin more strongly than monomer, so it is resolved into the descending edge of the
elution peak; the eluate-pool aggregate therefore rises when the column is more heavily
loaded, when a higher elution pH weakens the resolution, and when the pool is collected
further down the descending edge (a later stop-collect), with the load and pool-collection
effects acting together through their interaction. The worst case for pool aggregate is a
high load combined with a high elution pH and a late stop-collect. Host-cell protein, by
contrast, is weakly retained and is removed principally in the wash: a higher load/wash
conductivity displaces more HCP before the elution, improving clearance, while a heavier
load reduces clearance, and the two act together through the significant load × conductivity
interaction so that adequate wash conductivity matters most at high load. This is the
relationship depicted in @fig-cex and is the reason a multivariate operating region —
rather than independent one-dimensional ranges — is used to assure the aggregate and HCP
presented downstream. The step yield declines modestly at high load, where breakthrough
costs recovery, and is otherwise robust; the wash conductivity, which controls HCP, does
not affect the aggregate, so the two clearance functions are governed largely by different
parameters.

# Design space

The operating region (design space) is the multivariate region of the four well-controlled
CPPs over which the eluate-pool aggregate and HCP are held low enough that the drug
substance meets its ≤ `{python} f"{agg_acc_hi:g}"`% HMW aggregate and ≤ `{python} hcp_acc_hi`
ng/mg HCP limits (the latter after the anion-exchange polish), while the step yield remains
acceptable. Its two principal planes are protein load × wash conductivity, over which the
pool HCP is controlled (@fig-cex), and protein load × elution pH (with the stop-collect),
over which the pool aggregate is controlled (@fig-contours). The NOR of each parameter
(@tbl-param) — protein load
`{python} f"{load.nor[0]:g}–{load.nor[1]:g}"` g/L resin and load/wash conductivity
`{python} f"{wash.nor[0]:g}–{wash.nor[1]:g}"` mS/cm, with elution pH and the stop-collect
at their NORs — lies well inside the characterized region, which in turn lies within the
broader knowledge space bounded by the proven acceptable ranges. Movement within the
operating region is not a change, whereas movement outside it would require assessment
under the quality system [@amab2009; @ichq8]. Because the step yield is robust and the two
quality responses are governed by partly different parameters, the region is set jointly by
the aggregate and HCP constraints.

# Process capability and robustness

Cation exchange is the principal aggregate-reduction step of the process and a major
clearance step for host-cell protein, residual DNA and leached Protein A. A Monte-Carlo
simulation of `{python} f"{V['n_monte_carlo']:,}"` commercial-scale batches, with every
parameter varied within its NOR, was used to estimate the commercial-scale distributions
and process capability of the drug-substance CQAs to which this step contributes
(@tbl-cap). Capability is evaluated one-sided against the upper acceptance limit.

```{python}
#| output: asis
show(cap_for(CEX_CQAS), floatfmt=".2f")
```

: Commercial-scale process capability for the CQAs governed by the cation-exchange step. {#tbl-cap}

The drug-substance aggregate meets its ≤ `{python} f"{agg_acc_hi:g}"`% HMW limit with a
capability of **Cpk = `{python} f"{agg_cpk:.2f}"`**; as the only aggregate-reduction step,
cation exchange is the primary contributor to this outcome. The drug-substance HCP meets
its ≤ `{python} hcp_acc_hi` ng/mg limit with a capability of Cpk =
`{python} f"{hcp_cpk:.2f}"`, to which this step contributes a major reduction that the
anion-exchange step completes; and the residual DNA and leached Protein A are cleared to far
below their limits (Cpk = `{python} f"{dna_cpk:.1f}"` and `{python} f"{lpa_cpk:.0f}"`
respectively), with cation exchange providing modular clearance alongside the Protein A and
anion-exchange steps. The capability margins confirm that the NOR-bounded step contributes
robustly to in-specification drug substance at commercial scale.

# Parameter classification

Each parameter was classified on the A-Mab continuum from the demonstrated effects and the
operating-region risk (@tbl-class). The rationale is as follows.

- **Protein load — WC-CPP.** Significantly affects both the eluate-pool aggregate (its
  dominant factor) and the eluate-pool HCP, and participates in significant interactions
  with the elution pH, the stop-collect and the wash conductivity; it also governs the step
  yield. It is reliably held within the operating region by controlled load ratio, and is
  therefore a well-controlled CPP.
- **Load/wash conductivity — WC-CPP.** The dominant factor for HCP clearance (higher
  conductivity clears more HCP), with a significant load × conductivity interaction; it has
  no effect on aggregate. It is controlled by buffer preparation with in-process
  conductivity verification.
- **Elution pH, elution stop-collect — WC-CPP.** Each significantly affects the eluate-pool
  aggregate; both are reliably held within the operating region by controlled buffer
  preparation and a defined pool-collection criterion with in-process pH and UV monitoring.
- **Elution flow rate — GPP.** No meaningful impact on the CQAs or on performance was
  observed over the wide range studied.

Because every parameter that affects process performance (the step yield) also
significantly affects a product-quality CQA, there are no key process parameters (KPP) at
this step: the four multivariate parameters are well-controlled CPPs and the flow rate is a
general process parameter.

```{python}
#| output: asis
d = report_params(UO)[["Parameter", "Class", "Study"]]
show(d)
```

: Post-characterization parameter classification. {#tbl-class}

# Contribution to the control strategy

The cation-exchange step is the primary control point for high-molecular-weight aggregate
and a major control point for the process-related impurity load. Its contribution to the
overall control strategy comprises: control of the four WC-CPPs (protein load, load/wash
conductivity, elution pH and the elution stop-collect) to their NORs within the established
operating region; control of the elution flow rate as a general parameter; in-process
monitoring of the load ratio, pH, conductivity and UV profile and of the pool-collection
window; resin life-cycle control (**SOP-2008**); and release testing of the eluate-pool
aggregate, HCP, residual DNA and leached Protein A. The aggregate that can form during the
upstream low-pH hold is polished here, the host-cell protein reduced upstream by Protein A
is further reduced here and completed by anion exchange, and the residual DNA and leached
Protein A are cleared modularly across Protein A, cation exchange and anion exchange
(reported in the paired unit-operation reports and consolidated in **PCMR-001**).

# Discussion

The characterization quantifies the parameter–response relationships for the
cation-exchange polishing step, defines a robust multivariate operating region in the four
well-controlled CPPs, and classifies every parameter with a data-supported rationale. The
aggregate and pool-HCP response-surface models are adequate and predictive, and their
behaviour is consistent with established cation-exchange chromatography and with the A-Mab
prior knowledge, increasing confidence that the SDM is representative of commercial scale.
The step yield is governed by protein load and is otherwise robust. The principal
limitation is inherent to scale-down characterization: the absolute aggregate and HCP
clearance may shift modestly at scale and over the resin life-cycle, and the incoming
aggregate load depends on the upstream low-pH hold, which is why the operating region is
defined on the qualified SDM, challenged against a representative worst-case aggregate
feed, confirmed at commercial scale during Stage 2, and carried forward with in-process
monitoring and resin life-cycle control. The characterization did not identify any
parameter requiring the most stringent (CPP, as opposed to WC-CPP) control within the
studied ranges.

# Conclusions

The A-Mab cation-exchange polishing step is well understood and robust. The relationships
between the polishing parameters and the eluate-pool aggregate, the eluate-pool HCP and the
step yield are quantified by DoE; a multivariate operating region in the four
well-controlled CPPs is established; every parameter range is justified by data; and the
drug-substance CQAs governed by the step meet acceptance at commercial scale, with the step
being the principal contributor to the drug-substance aggregate capability of Cpk =
`{python} f"{agg_cpk:.2f}"`. The operating region, parameter classifications and proven
acceptable ranges provide the basis for the Stage 2 operating ranges and the drug-substance
control strategy. This report rolls up into the Process Characterization Master Report
(**PCMR-001**) and provides the parameter risk basis for the post-characterization process
risk assessment.
